action: Equinor partners and suppliers: no action required yet. Follow Equinor's official updates, treat unexpected emails that appear to come from Equinor with extra care, and confirm payment or access requests by phone.
exec: A major European energy supplier reports a cyberattack on its IT systems has been stopped; operations are reported unaffected.
plain: Norwegian energy company Equinor said on November 17 it had detected a cyberattack on some of its computer systems. Its updated notice says the attack has been stopped, production ran as usual and there are no signs data was stolen or altered.
summary: Equinor said it detected a cyberattack on its IT systems on November 17; production is unaffected. On November 18 it saw no risk of the attack spreading. In its November 20 notice, as relayed by MarketScreener, Equinor says the attack has been stopped, was handled with national security authorities and reported to police, and there are no signs data was stolen or altered. No attacker named.
title: Equinor cyberattack on IT systems stopped, company says; production unaffected

validation.note: Company statement, Reuters, The Record, Cybersecurity Dive and TechRadar (relaying Equinor's updated notice).

review.note: Compared title, date 17 Nov, stopped notice 20 Nov, production unaffected, no signs of data theft, police and national security authorities, no attacker named against MarketScreener, Reuters via AOL, The Record, Cybersecurity Dive, Riviera and TechRadar.
